patch_description:
The current approach uses 8 Dirichlet restarts, 30,000 annealing iterations each, an interior-biased Dirichlet concentration of 1.15, soft-min scale cooling from 0.0100 to 0.00065, and directional local polishing. Its main limitation is that the final local search only tests a finite collection of directions.

This version uses a more diverse deterministic initialization portfolio: low-concentration boundary-seeking Dirichlet samples, moderate interior samples, and jittered structured lattice templates. Annealing is shortened to 14,000 iterations per restart but uses 14 restarts and includes occasional two-point perturbations to escape poor oriented-matroid cells. The principal new refinement is an exact coordinate-wise maximin linear-program step implemented by half-plane clipping in the simplex. With all other points fixed, every signed triangle determinant involving one movable point is affine, so this step finds the best feasible location for that point within its current orientation cell rather than merely probing several directions. This produces substantially stronger final balancing of tight triangle constraints while retaining deterministic behavior and graceful finite-value checks.
